candidate.name: intraday_directional_amount_timing_spread_238m
candidate.mechanism: Difference between the fixed-session clock centers of transaction amount attached to positive and negative within-half one-minute close returns
candidate.formula: For 238 within-half returns with destination amount A_k and fixed chronological coordinate u_k=k/237, compute U=sum A_k*1[r_k>0], D=sum A_k*1[r_k<0], T_up=sum u_k*A_k*1[r_k>0]/U, T_down=sum u_k*A_k*1[r_k<0]/D, and score=T_up-T_down.
candidate.zero_rule: Exact zero returns contribute to neither directional mass; zero destination amounts remain exact zeros. Require every return and destination amount, finite positive U and D, and use no epsilon, pseudocount, minimum directional count, threshold, or dropped source row.
candidate.fixed_grid: Exactly 240 closes at 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00, producing 119 returns per half and 238 pooled chronological positions; exclude required raw 09:30 and never form a lunch pair.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_up_move_amount_share_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: both split destination-bar transaction amount by the sign of the same 238 within-half returns
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor measures the positive-direction share of total nonzero-return amount and discards clock position. Campaign089 separately normalizes positive and negative amount and retains only their clock-center difference; independent scaling of either directional mass changes the share but not Campaign089.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_amount_center_of_mass_240m, intraday_amount_clock_dispersion_240m, intraday_amount_profile_serial_persistence_240m, intraday_amount_local_peak_density_238p, intraday_above_median_amount_longest_run_240m, and intraday_amount_path_efficiency_238p
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all use the intraday ordering of transaction amount
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those factors are direction-blind univariate summaries of the complete amount path. Campaign089 conditions the destination amount path on positive versus negative close-return signs and takes a signed difference of two conditional centers. Direction-label swaps preserve every listed amount-only value but negate or otherwise change Campaign089.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: late_return_30m and late_amount_share_30m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all can respond to activity or returns near the session end
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The late-window factors select one fixed 30-minute subwindow and measure its marginal return or amount share. Campaign089 uses every one of the 238 return positions, chooses no late threshold, and compares positive-versus-negative conditional timing centers.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: afternoon_signed_amount_efficiency_120m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: both are directional transaction-amount mechanisms with higher interpreted as buy-side pressure
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Afternoon efficiency selects only the afternoon and weights amount by signed return magnitude relative to absolute-return-weighted amount. Campaign089 uses both halves, ignores every nonzero return magnitude, and measures when directional amount arrives rather than its signed efficiency.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_amount_lead_return_correlation_238p and intraday_volatility_activity_lead_lag_asymmetry_236p
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all connect activity with returns on an ordered grid
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The lead-lag factors ask whether earlier activity predicts a later signed or absolute return using adjacent pairs and correlations. Campaign089 is contemporaneous at each destination bar, estimates no correlation, and uses the full-session clock only as a conditional timing coordinate.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_amount_volatility_coupling_238p and intraday_amount_price_discovery_alignment_js_238p
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all connect destination activity to close-return observations
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those factors use absolute return magnitude through Pearson co-movement or a Jensen-Shannon participation profile. Campaign089 is invariant to every magnitude change preserving return signs and compares two signed conditional clock centers rather than magnitude alignment.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_return_sign_run_imbalance_238p, intraday_bar_direction_continuity_238p, and intraday_day_over_day_directional_return_agreement_238b
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The sign factors ignore amount and measure runs, adjacent body continuity, or cross-day agreement. Campaign089 ignores sign adjacency and prior days; identical sign paths with different within-sign amount timing have identical prior values but different Campaign089 values.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_directional_price_impact_asymmetry_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: both distinguish positive from negative return bars and read amount
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Directional impact compares return displacement per unit activity and therefore depends on magnitude. Campaign089 contains no return magnitude or reciprocal activity term and measures only the relative clock arrival of separately normalized directional amount.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_zero_return_amount_intensity_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: both specify exact-zero return amount semantics
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Zero-return intensity makes unchanged-price activity the signal. Campaign089 leaves zero-return amount outside both directional centers; changing only that amount leaves Campaign089 unchanged.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_range_amount_profile_alignment_js_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: the preceding terminal numeric factor compares amount allocation over the fixed clock
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Campaign087 aligns a 240-bar amount distribution with same-bar high-low range mass and reads no close. Campaign089 reads no high or low, uses 238 destination amounts, and compares clock centers conditional on close-return sign without Jensen-Shannon divergence.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_bipower_jump_variation_share_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: the latest terminal numeric factor uses the same 238 within-half close returns
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Campaign088 is direction- and amount-invariant and decomposes quadratic variation with adjacent bipower products. Campaign089 ignores all return magnitudes, reads destination amount, uses no adjacent return pair, and is sign-antisymmetric.
